v12_citation_occurrences.context_latex: An audio interval can meet both first-delivery deadlines yet become temporarily unavailable after a compatible feedback update. In streaming speech correction, a selected correction supplies the input to later recognition~\cite{vu2026streamcorrect}. Here, trusted feedback is feedback accepted by the original protected selection process. In the actual execution of Figure~\ref{fig:continuity_case}(a), a complete interval is displayed within two seconds (D2), then withdrawn despite a still-valid dependency path. Identical text returns through certified delivery within eight seconds (C8), leaving a 2.176-s gap between the two timely first deliveries. We call this an \emph{avoidable withdrawal}: an update retracts a delivered whole view that it still supports. The client loses progress that the revision did not refute.

An immutable audio stream supplies a protected selection path producing \emph{Canonical} facts and a \emph{Private} path computing and displaying provisional hypotheses. These are logical roles. The core runtime assigns them to separate Private and Authority workers. The native runtime uses two complete original recognizer--corrector workers; either can execute a selected-input or conditional full call. Selection can change the next call's input: StreamCorrect feeds its chosen correction into subsequent ASR~\cite{vu2026streamcorrect}. We coordinate this dependency as the paths advance asynchronously.

StreamCorrect supplies a concrete recursive feedback task \cite{vu2026streamcorrect}. For complete closed state $P$ and accepted audio $X$, expose its recognition boundary as \begin{equation} A(P,X)=(B,M), \end{equation} where $B$ contains ordered beam candidates and $M$ the engine state and inputs needed by original Correct/Update. Candidate order, prompts, returned token IDs, selection, and update rules remain intact.

Input-confirmed full calls improve timely service while preserving the original feedback task. On eight previously unused speakers, RevTrace raises audio coverage meeting both deadlines from 40.6\% to 93.9\% and whole-run passes from zero to ten of sixteen (Table~\ref{tab:native_full_confirm}). A paired speaker bootstrap, keeping both timing repeats together, gives a duration-weighted gain of 53.3 percentage points (95\% CI [44.8, 59.6]; 20,000 resamples). All eight source-paired gains are positive, ranging from 27.8 to 61.4 percentage points. The StreamCorrect adaptation retains original learned correction and feedback, using fixed 500-ms inputs, no VAD, and FP32 execution~\cite{vu2026streamcorrect}. Both author-built policies have two complete workers, the same ASR early-view Consumer and neural warmup. Conservative execution waits for selected parent feedback; RevTrace starts conditional full calls and retains them when their complete inputs are confirmed.

Whisper-Streaming converts an offline recognizer into incremental service using LocalAgreement~\cite{machacek2023whisperstreaming}. StreamCorrect adds learned correction and feeds selected corrections into subsequent recognition~\cite{vu2026streamcorrect}. RevTrace retains that selection and feedback behavior in its controlled native adapter; its contribution concerns the asynchronous execution and consumption around the feedback boundary. It does not introduce a better acoustic model or train a new corrector.

v12_citation_occurrences.context_latex: Before acknowledgment, synchronized frames bind parent/next states, request identity, selected complete result, and receipt; recorded deltas must reconstruct the state. Group-ready commit shares synchronization among validated sessions without a collection timeout or cross-session atomic transaction. Uncertain append/application outcomes block writes. Write-ahead recovery~\cite{mohan1992aries} reconstructs facts and identities; the native extension binds this to original correction calls.
